description: Controlled Artemis III PDF stress set derived from demos/rag_retrieval_explanation/data/artemis.pdf. It contains 10 direct-evidence questions and 30 short passages. Interaction labels are intentionally omitted for this qualitative PDF-oriented evaluation.

passages.title: Artemis III first crewed lunar surface mission
passages.text: The Artemis III mission is described as the first human mission to the surface of the Moon in the 21st century.

passages.title: Apollo legacy
passages.text: The report says Artemis III will build on the legacy of Apollo and begin a modern era of human exploration and development in deep space.

passages.title: Lunar surface science value
passages.text: The lunar surface is presented as an ideal location for answering fundamental planetary science questions.

passages.title: Seven Artemis III science objectives
passages.text: The seven overarching Artemis III science objectives are understanding planetary processes, understanding the character and origin of lunar polar volatiles, interpreting the impact history of the Earth-Moon system, revealing the record of the ancient sun and astronomical environment, observing the universe and local space environment from a unique location, conducting experimental science in the lunar environment, and investigating and mitigating exploration risks.

passages.title: Science traceability matrix
passages.text: The Science Goals and Investigations mapped to the Artemis objectives were used to populate a Science Traceability Matrix.

passages.title: Investigation prioritization
passages.text: The Science Definition Team prioritized investigations by considering both compelling science and whether Artemis III presented an enabling opportunity.

passages.title: South polar operational benefits
passages.text: The Moon's south polar region was selected because it offers two clear operational benefits: access to persistently illuminated areas and potential access to surface-accessible volatile deposits.

passages.title: South polar region definition
passages.text: The report defines the Moon's south polar region as the area within 6 degrees of latitude from the lunar south pole.

passages.title: Persistent illumination
passages.text: Some lunar south polar areas are illuminated for more than 200 days per year, offering operational benefits such as solar power and reduced lunar night duration.

passages.title: Artemis III surface stay
passages.text: Artemis III astronauts are expected to spend up to 6.5 days on the lunar surface, living inside the HLS crew cabin before launching back to lunar orbit.

passages.title: HLS design awards
passages.text: NASA awarded Blue Origin, Dynetics, and SpaceX contracts to begin refining Human Landing System designs.

passages.title: Crew transfer options
passages.text: The Artemis III crew may rendezvous with the lander at the Gateway or may board the lander directly from Orion.

passages.title: Moonwalk requirement and goal
passages.text: NASA established a minimum requirement of one planned EVA and one contingency EVA for Artemis III, while the goal is at least four moonwalks with reserves for a fifth contingency EVA.

passages.title: EVA preparation
passages.text: Each Artemis III EVA will begin with tool selection and preparation for investigations performed on that EVA.

passages.title: EVA duration constraints
passages.text: The number and duration of Artemis III EVAs will depend on HLS downmass and the allocation of resources for spacesuits and portable life support systems.

passages.title: Candidate sample return mass
passages.text: The candidate Artemis III sample program totals 83 kg of lunar samples, slightly more than the 64 kg average sample return mass from the Apollo missions.

passages.title: Candidate sample types
passages.text: The candidate sample program includes contingency bulk samples, rake samples, hand samples, sealed drill cores, sealed surface samples, and regolith surface samples.

passages.title: Sealed core samples
passages.text: Sealed core samples can preserve stratigraphic and structural information while reducing volatile loss and contamination.

passages.title: Apollo-style geology training
passages.text: The report recommends that astronauts participate in an Apollo-style geology and planetary science course and that an Earth-based Artemis III Science Mission Center provide real-time support.

passages.title: Geologic context observations
passages.text: The optimal sample return program is built on geologic context observations by well-trained astronauts aided by modern tools and real-time communication with scientists on Earth.

passages.title: Astronaut field training
passages.text: Astronaut geology field training teaches what samples to collect, how much of each to collect, and how to document and store them for return to Earth.

passages.title: In situ instrumentation classes
passages.text: In situ instrumentation is described as beneficial for sampling, volatile monitoring, geophysics objectives, down-hole monitoring, and geotechnical characterization.

passages.title: In situ imaging recommendation
passages.text: NASA should ensure that in situ imaging capability is available during EVA to document exploration, sampling, and instrument deployment.

passages.title: Sample triage
passages.text: In situ geochemistry and mineralogy data can help the crew and ground control teams decide which scientifically valuable samples should be returned to Earth.

passages.title: Long-lived power and communications
passages.text: Several prioritized Artemis III investigations would be maximally enabled by a long-lived power source and communications capability for deployed experiments.

passages.title: ALSEP-like packages
passages.text: NASA should pursue long-lived power and communications to enable networked operation of ALSEP-like packages at multiple landing sites.

passages.title: Pre-positioned science assets
passages.text: NASA should consider pre-positioning science assets near the Artemis III landing site, such as an inert cache of tools and instruments or instrumented landers or rovers for environmental monitoring.

passages.title: Geodetic control importance
passages.text: Accurate geodetic control directly affects the accuracy of spatial data analysis and intercomparison, which is vital to both mission planning and scientific analysis.

passages.title: Lunar mapping datasets
passages.text: Recent lunar datasets from LRO, Chandrayaan-1, GRAIL, LADEE, and SELENE provide a comprehensive modern view of the Moon.

passages.title: Cartographic and time controls
passages.text: The report recommends standards for cartographic and time controls, including high-fidelity time coding for surface measurements synchronized with Earth in UTC.

cases.question: Which Artemis mission is described as the first human mission to the Moon's surface in the 21st century?
cases.gold_answer: Artemis III is described as the first human mission to the Moon's surface in the 21st century.

cases.question: What are the seven overarching Artemis III science objectives?
cases.gold_answer: They are understanding planetary processes, lunar polar volatiles, Earth-Moon impact history, the ancient sun and astronomical environment, observing the universe and local space environment, experimental science in the lunar environment, and exploration risk mitigation.

cases.question: Which two operational benefits led to selecting the Moon's south polar region for Artemis III?
cases.gold_answer: The south polar region offers access to persistently illuminated areas and potential access to surface-accessible volatile deposits.

cases.question: How long are Artemis III astronauts expected to spend on the lunar surface?
cases.gold_answer: Artemis III astronauts are expected to spend up to 6.5 days on the lunar surface.

cases.question: What is NASA's minimum EVA requirement and EVA goal for Artemis III?
cases.gold_answer: The minimum is one planned EVA and one contingency EVA, while the goal is at least four moonwalks with reserves for a fifth contingency EVA.

cases.question: What total lunar sample mass does the candidate Artemis III sample program propose?
cases.gold_answer: The candidate Artemis III sample program proposes 83 kg of lunar samples.

cases.question: What training and mission support does the report recommend for Artemis III astronauts doing sample collection?
cases.gold_answer: It recommends Apollo-style geology and planetary science training, plus real-time support from an Earth-based Artemis III Science Mission Center.

cases.question: Which Artemis III science activities would benefit from in situ instrumentation?
cases.gold_answer: In situ instrumentation would benefit sampling, volatile monitoring, geophysics objectives, down-hole monitoring, and geotechnical characterization.

cases.question: What capability would maximally enable several prioritized deployed Artemis III investigations?
cases.gold_answer: A long-lived power source and communications capability would maximally enable several prioritized deployed investigations.

cases.question: Why is accurate geodetic control important for Artemis III data products?
cases.gold_answer: Accurate geodetic control improves spatial data analysis and intercomparison, which is vital for mission planning and scientific analysis.
